chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Amr ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever bequeaths a share (sahm) of his wealth, it is a share out of ten." It is likely that the narrator erred, and he actually heard this regarding one who bequeaths a part (juz') of his wealth, and he assumed it applied to one who bequeaths a share, or he may have believed that 'part' and 'share' are the same, so he narrated it according to what he thought.

key_terms.الْجُزْءَ وَالسَّهْمَ: The part and the share (conceptual comparison)
key_terms.سَهْمٍ: Share (specifically interpreted as one-tenth in this context)
key_terms.عَشَرَةٍ: Ten (referring to the denominator for the share)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a bequest described as 'a share' (sahm) of wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the legal interpretation of an ambiguous bequest using the term 'sahm' (share), ruling it as one-tenth (1/10) of the estate. The text includes a scholarly note suggesting the narrator may have confused the term 'sahm' with 'juz'' (part), or considered them synonymous, leading to this specific interpretation. This reflects the Shia juristic approach to resolving linguistic ambiguities in wills, ensuring the testator's intent is preserved while maintaining fairness among heirs.
